thread:
maya: Quick heads-up — on the int4 bring-up today I noticed an odd asymmetry. Codegen prompts look fine but instruction-style prompts (Q/A, summarization) have a consistent quality dip, hallucinations in >10% of samples.

oliver: That matches an earlier smoke I saw. Could be tokenization+quant interaction or sampling distribution shift. Do we have per-prompt-type metrics?

sasha: Not yet. I did a quick pass: perplexity increase is small, but exact-match and factuality scores drop on instruction tasks. Link to small run: https://ci/redwood/runs/1767

maya: I dumped 200 failing pairs to /mnt/curation/quant-int4-fails-200.json. Many are short instruction prompts with enumerations and follow-ups.

oliver: Can you paste a couple here?

maya: Sure — examples pasted below:
```
Prompt: "List the steps to rotate an ssh key on linux and explain what each step does."
Expected: bullet steps with commands + brief rationale
Model (int8): correct
Model (int4): invents extra steps and claims commands not present on linux
```

sasha: Hmm. Two hypotheses: 1) dequantization error in attention weights for short instruction tokens; 2) our sampling temperature config for int4 fallback is different and causing overconfident completions.

anna: We should triage with stratified promptset. I can spin up a label batch for the 200 fails and a matched control of 200 passes. Need to know dedupe rules for this batch (we don't want many near-duplicates).

maya: For dedupe, use fuzzyhash threshold 0.82 and discard paraphrase duplicates with >0.9 embed cosine. Keep source metadata.

curation-bot: added task curation/3456 to labeler queue (owner: sasha) — 200 items, priority: high.

sasha: I'll own the label batch, will tag each fail with root-cause categories: tokenization, hallucination, context-truncation, sampling-artifact, other.

raj: I'll re-run the quant benchmark with matched samplers. Command I used (feel free to copy):
```
python tools/quant_bench.py --model rdx-3b --quant int4 --seed 42 --prompts /mnt/curation/stratified_prompts.json --metrics factuality,exact_match,perp --out runs/1767-quant
```

oliver: Also add a run with fixed seed+greedy decoding to isolate sampling vs model degradation.

anna: For golden set updates — do we append failing items to the golden guard set or create a distinct int4-regression suite? I prefer a separate int4-regression suite to avoid contaminating general golden.

maya: Agreed. Create golden/int4-regression.json with the 200 verified fails plus 200 control items. We'll run CI against that on every quant PR.

curation-bot: golden suite created: golden/int4-regression.json (size: 400). CI integration scheduled for quant branch protection.

raj: One more: let's snapshot tokenizer outputs for int8 vs int4 for the failing prompts — if tokenization differs that's a red flag. Use:`python tools/dump_tokens.py --model rdx-3b --prompts file.json --out tok-diff.json`

sasha: I'll coordinate labeling and run an initial root-cause pass tonight. If >60% are hallucinations tied to enumerations, we should prioritize sampling config adjustments + add more enumerated prompts to the promptset.

oliver: If it's attention quant noise, we may need to try different kernel ordering or a per-layer calibration (int4 fast path tweak). I'll file an infra issue if labels point that way.

anna: Owner matrix: sasha -> labeling/gold, raj -> bench+token-dump, oliver -> infra investigation, maya -> promptset curation + dedupe rules. I'll update the tracker.

maya: Thanks. Quick ask to @labeling team: please avoid bulk merges of paraphrase variants until dedupe-0.82 is enforced.

curation-bot: @labeling notified.

oliver: Plan for immediate mitigation: run CI with greedy decoding for int4 to prevent sampling-induced hallucinations, and block rolling int4 for instruction-heavy endpoints until root cause confirmed.

sasha: Acknowledged. Will have labeled batch + preliminary tags in ~6 hours.

maya: Great, thanks all. Will follow up with a short summary and next-steps after labels. :thumbsup:
